items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Bernie Richter. He's a cello player, the biggest hustler that's ever hit the city of New Orleans... Bernie's been very sick lately... Bernie plays well.

ctx.x: I played the other night. I moved on to- You know, you can tell him. The other night I moved that damn instrument outside, I said I was ready to fall to pieces. That's right. And I didn't work hard, because, I mean, it was not a hard job.

Well, he stuck with me. If I don't- If I don't help him get his instrument, he can't go to a job. So, by the time he booked a job, he got to put a bass on. Put the bass on top of the barbara hub. Incidentally, that bass, I told my sister, I said, you didn't like bass fiddles around the house at all. Oh, this symphony boy there last night asked me, he says, if you ever have any instruments, he says, I'd like to buy them. I'd like to buy them. I told him, I says, in my mind, I said to myself, he ain't getting paid,…

Well, Bernie, Bernie, no, the story of that he drove a cab was that he was so disgusted with the kickbacks that these theater orchestras were making that he just got out of the business. Yeah, yeah. And he says, I'll go drive a cab to make a livelihood. And that's what he did for quite a while. And then he came down here and had an audition with the Hillsburg one. Hillsburg.
